chunk_map.heading: 1. Treat CI as feedback into the loop, not a gate to pass
2. Fan out review; converge on the pattern
3. Tier by blast radius. Make the Tier-1 case on your own PRs
Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice
4. Eval latency is part of the loop
Cherny pairs a fast check with a slow one
5. Skills don't just live in your kit. Promote them into the CI surface
The skill catalogue scales: plan time to company-wide
6. Get out fast. Learn from real customers safely
Agents need the outer loop's signal too
Where this fits in your AE101 arc

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-read all 14 chunks this session against the live file. Closest candidates: chunk 3 line 21 'A single reviewer reading 30 agent-drafted PRs a day skims. The best refuse the trade.' — 'the trade' is the speed/thoroughness trade-off named in the same sentence, same chunk, not vague-with-full-history. Chunk 5 header (line 35) 'Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice' names 'the slice' before its own body explains it (line 37 'auto-merging the lowest-risk slice') — header-then-explanation inside the SAME chunk, not a forward reference. Chunk 9 header 'The skill catalogue scales' likewise introduces 'skill catalogue' before its own body (line 63) defines it, same-chunk. Grepped body for bare pronoun-heavy openers ('This ', 'That ', 'It ') at chunk starts: none found outside these same-chunk cases. Collective callback in the closer (chunk 12, line 85, 'These engineers run the same loop') resolves against every practitioner named across the file by that point in the sequential read.

Grepped body this session for 'opening lecture|earlier module|prior module|the prework|see below|above|below|further down|at the top of|coming up|in this module': only hit is line 5 'None require permission from above to start trying' (idiomatic 'from higher authority', not a file-position pointer). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0, module-flag branch: subtitle (line 3) 'Read after you've shipped your second skill' gates the read BEFORE body line 5 claims 'You finished M6 owning the loop at your desk. Two sessions of the same task, gap diagnosis, a second skill in `~/.claude/skills/`, one rule cut from `./CLAUDE.local.md`.' Re-verified every named beat against the CURRENT M6 files this session (both read in full, not carried from cache): two sessions / gap diagnosis / rule cut are all live — `spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` line 25 'You walk in holding two sessions of the same task', line 14-15 the memory/verifier/skill diagnosis + rule cut LOs; exercise Phase 1 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' (lines 35-42). 'A second skill in `~/.claude/skills/`' is NOT an in-module M6 artefact per the module's own Artefact-contracts table (line 123): the module produces a 'Workflow-skills handoff prompt' consumed by 'The student's own later sessions: run cold to study their stack, diagram recurring shapes, author a skill per shape' — the skill ships AFTER the module closes, when that prompt is run. A 2026-08-19 maintainer note at `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/skill-stacking.md:179` documents the identical seam for a sibling file ('The 2026-08-01 M6 cut removed the in-module second-skill build: M6's close now produces a handoff prompt the student runs later to author skills, so no skill ships inside the module'). This file's own subtitle already conditions the read on that later event having happened, so the beat this file references is real and module-sanctioned, just deferred past M6's formal close rather than produced inside it — not the dead-beat failure shape (a beat cut with no home anywhere). PASS. Note: a prior verdict on this same row cited `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/autumn-gaps.md` as corroboration — that file does not exist (`ls` exit 2, confirmed this session). That citation is discarded, not reused; this evidence is independently re-derived from the live files.

Closest candidate, chunk 1 (shortest, lines 7-10): header + one three-sentence paragraph carrying a complete, self-standing claim ('A failing CI run is signal... Each red build sharpens the next session.'). Not a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. All 14 chunks re-checked this session: every one carries at least one full paragraph plus (for numbered-move chunks) a named practitioner example or a 'Try this Monday' action; none is orphaned.

Chunk 4 header (line 29): '3. Tier by blast radius. Make the Tier-1 case on your own PRs.' Chunk 4's own content (lines 29-34) delivers the tiering definition and Intercom's stats, but never delivers the header's second clause — the 'make the case' action only appears in chunk 5's 'Try this Monday' (line 41), under a differently-topicked header ('Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice', framed around Stripe's CONTRASTING bet). Compared against the file's other five move headers, re-checked this session: Move 1 (line 7), Move 2 (line 19, both clauses fulfilled same-chunk), Move 4 (line 43), Move 5 (line 55, fulfilled same-chunk via AGENTS.md/rules-files/pre-commit-hooks), Move 6 (line 69, fulfilled same-chunk) each keep their promise inside their own chunk. Move 3 alone bundles an imperative into its header and defers it to a different chunk — an outlier against the file's own pattern.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Fold a 'make the case' action into chunk 4 itself (mirroring Move 5), or trim the header to 'Tier by blast radius' and let chunk 5's Try-this-Monday stand without an unclaimed promise pointing at it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*'` against the body this session (18 bolded spans total) and assigned each to its chunk. No menu/lookup-surface carve-out applies: this file is a sequential essay meant to be read once ('Take-home reading' / 'Read after you've shipped your second skill'), not a scanned reference table — per §9's own scope test 'a reference page's narrative preamble is still narrative,' and this whole file is that narrative. Six of 14 chunks exceed the ≤1 budget: chunk 2 (lines 13/15/17, THREE), chunk 3 (lines 23/27, two), chunk 5 (lines 37/41, two), chunk 7 (lines 51/53, two), chunk 9 (lines 63/65/67, THREE), chunk 11 (lines 77/79/81, THREE). None of these bolded spans (practitioner-name leads or the recurring 'Try this Monday.') is a named law/governor/coined term/checklist-item name in the rule's sense — they read as attribution styling and a recurring action-cue, i.e. narrative/recognition-beat prose the rule bans from bold. Chunks 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 correctly carry ≤1 bold each, confirming this file's own pattern treats the six flagged chunks as the outlier, not house style. Rule question for the maintainer: even if 'Try this Monday.' is read as a deliberate recurring widget-handle (like the 'Read:' mode-word in the menu carve-out), the co-occurring practitioner-name bolds still push all six chunks over budget on their own.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Pick one bolded handle per chunk (most naturally 'Try this Monday.') and drop the practitioner-name bolding to plain text; where two practitioners share one chunk (9, 11), either accept two bolds as genuine content or split the '##' so each gets its own budget.
